convention.local_space: metres, y increases INTO the room
convention.back_wall: the wall the fixture touches is at y = 0
convention.origin: back-left corner of the footprint, given in viewBox coords
convention.rotation: orthogonal only — N=0, E=90, S=180, W=270 degrees
convention.mirror: scale(-1,1) about the footprint centre for handed pieces
convention.footprint_shape: rect, circle or L. Where circle, w == d is the diameter and the corners of that square are free floor. Where L, footprint.cells gives the rectangles actually occupied and w/d are only the bounding box
convention.anchor: wall_back (one wall behind), corner (two walls meeting at the origin), free, or center

fixtures.label: Shower stall
fixtures.notes: 0.90 m square is the PH mid-market minimum. Many mid-market baths have no stall at all — see tabo_set and floor_drain.

fixtures.label: Dining counter divider

stretch.how: extend the run; one seat per 0.60 m of length

clearance.reason: chair pulled out, plus room to pass behind it
working at the counter from the kitchen side

fixtures.notes: The divider that doubles as the dining table — one piece of millwork doing the wall's job and the table's job, which is how a compact PH plan gets a dining area without spending a room on it. 0.60 m of base cabinet plus a 0.30 m unsupported OVERHANG, marked by the dashed line across it. That overhang is the whole difference from counter_peninsula: without knee room you are perching at a snack bar, not sitting at a table. 0.38 m is more comfortable if the plan can spare it. Seats go on the living side only — the kitchen side stays working counter.

fixtures.label: Peninsula counter (mini-bar)

stretch.how: extend the run; stools space out to suit, one per 0.60 m

clearance.reason: stool pulled out, plus room to pass behind it
working at the counter from the kitchen side

fixtures.notes: The most common divider in the precedent set — 26 of 79 records separate kitchen from dining or living with a counter and stools and NOTHING else, and PH vendor plans often label it MINI-BAR outright. Footprint is the counter; the stools are drawn beyond it because that is where they are, which shows the real cost: 0.60 m of counter but about 1.65 m of floor. One end normally meets the kitchen counter or a wall — it is a peninsula, not an island. At 0.60 m deep there is no knee room, so this is a perch: use counter_dining_divider where the counter has to serve as the dining table.

fixtures.label: Compact dining table, 4-seat
fixtures.notes: A 0.90 m square seating 4 — the set for a dining zone that is a gap between rooms rather than a room. Square rather than rectangular on purpose: it takes the same floor from either direction, so it drops into a leftover space without the plan having to decide which way the dining runs. Pair it with counter_peninsula where the kitchen edge does the dividing.

fixtures.label: Kitchen counter run

stretch.how: extend the run; the nosing line and overhead-cabinet dashed line stretch with it

clearance.reason: working at the counter with a door behind you

fixtures.notes: Dashed line is the overhead cabinet. Trim rather than delete when it meets a doorway.

fixtures.label: Kitchen counter, L-shaped

stretch.how: each leg extends independently from the corner, which stays fixed at the origin

clearance.reason: working at the counter with a door behind you

fixtures.notes: The most common PH kitchen form — 29 of the 79 precedent records describe the counter as an L, against 2 galley and 2 single-wall. Wants a CORNER, two walls meeting at the origin. `w`/`d` are the bounding box; `cells` gives the two legs. The dashed square at the corner is the blind cabinet, reachable from one leg only — so put the sink on one leg and the range on the other rather than either side of the corner. Handed: mirror for the other hand.

fixtures.label: Kitchen sink (double bowl)
fixtures.notes: Sits IN the counter run — overlap with kitchen_counter is expected, not a collision.

fixtures.label: Range / cooktop (4 burner)
fixtures.notes: Sits in the counter run like the sink.

fixtures.label: Coffee table
fixtures.notes: Free-standing: sits about 0.40 m off the sofa front, not on a wall.

fixtures.label: Sofa, L-shaped (sectional)
fixtures.notes: Wants a CORNER — two walls meeting at the origin — not one wall. `w` and `d` are only the bounding box; `cells` gives what is actually occupied, and the inner corner of the L is free floor, which is where the coffee table goes. Handed: mirror to put the return on the other side. On a small PH living room this seats more than a 3-seat plus armchairs and leaves more floor, which is why it is everywhere.

fixtures.label: TV console (empty)
fixtures.notes: The stand on its own. Use tv_on_console for the usual case.

fixtures.label: TV on console
fixtures.notes: Footprint is the CONSOLE — the set sits on top and adds no floor area. The thin bar is the screen seen from above; the small tab behind it is the pedestal foot, which is what distinguishes this from tv_wall_mounted at a glance. Put it on the wall the sofa faces.

fixtures.label: Car
fixtures.notes: Sedan / small SUV. A carport that fits the box but not the door clearance is the classic PH plan failure — that is what the clearance entries are for.

fixtures.label: Floor drain
fixtures.notes: Every wet room needs one. Set at the low point of the floor slope.

fixtures.label: Lavatory (pedestal)
fixtures.notes: Use where the bath is too tight for a counter run.

fixtures.label: Tabo and pail set
fixtures.notes: The wet-corner alternative to a shower stall. A bath that cannot take a 0.90 m stall is not automatically undersized — a great many PH mid-market baths are designed around this instead.

fixtures.label: Water heater (wall)
fixtures.notes: Wall-mounted, no floor area. Draw over the shower or basin wall.

fixtures.label: Small cabinet
fixtures.notes: Maid's room and utility storage where a full wardrobe will not fit.

fixtures.label: Walk-in closet unit
fixtures.notes: Two facing runs need 0.90 m between them, which is what sets the minimum WIC width at about 2.10 m.

fixtures.label: Bar stool
fixtures.notes: For placing stools individually where the peninsula symbol's own three do not suit.
